DISTRICT.comment: Demographic and economic statistics for each of the 77 districts (okresy) of the Czech Republic in the mid-1990s. A district is a local administrative area; districts are grouped into 8 regions.

columns.A2: District name, written without Czech accents, e.g. 'Benesov', 'Kladno', 'Brno - mesto'. 'Hl.m. Praha' is the capital city, Prague.
columns.A3: Region the district belongs to. One of 8 regions: 'Prague', 'central Bohemia', 'south Bohemia', 'west Bohemia', 'north Bohemia', 'east Bohemia', 'south Moravia', 'north Moravia'. Prague is a region of its own with a single district.
columns.A4: Number of inhabitants (population) of the district. 42,821 to 1,204,953; the largest is Hl.m. Praha.
columns.A5: Number of municipalities in the district with fewer than 500 inhabitants. 0 to 151.
columns.A6: Number of municipalities in the district with 500 to 1,999 inhabitants. 0 to 70.
columns.A7: Number of municipalities in the district with 2,000 to 9,999 inhabitants. 0 to 20.
columns.A8: Number of municipalities in the district with 10,000 or more inhabitants. 0 to 5.
columns.A9: Number of cities (towns) in the district. 1 to 11.
columns.A10: Ratio of urban inhabitants: the percentage of the population living in towns. 33.9 to 100.0; 100 for the four city districts (Hl.m. Praha, Brno - mesto, Plzen - mesto, Ostrava - mesto).
columns.A11: Average monthly salary in the district, in Czech crowns (CZK). 8,110 to 12,541; highest in Hl.m. Praha, lowest in Bruntal.
columns.A12: Unemployment rate in 1995, as a percentage (0.2 means 0.2%). 0.2 to 7.3. Unknown (NULL) for Jesenik.
columns.A13: Unemployment rate in 1996, as a percentage. 0.43 to 9.4.
columns.A14: Number of entrepreneurs per 1,000 inhabitants. 81 to 167.
columns.A15: Number of crimes committed in the district in 1995 (a count, not a rate). 818 to 85,677. Unknown (NULL) for Jesenik.
columns.A16: Number of crimes committed in the district in 1996 (a count, not a rate). 888 to 99,107.
